audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for widow offering, temple prediction, apocalyptic warnings, Jerusalem surrounded, Son of Humanity, fig tree, watchfulness.

verses.restored: Looking up, he saw rich people casting their gifts into the treasury.

familiar.text: And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury.

modern.text: Then Jesus looked up and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury,

original.text: Ἀναβλέψας δὲ εἶδεν τοὺς βάλλοντας ⸂εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον τὰ δῶρα αὐτῶν⸃ πλουσίους.

verses.restored: He saw a certain poor widow casting there two small coins.

familiar.text: And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites.

modern.text: and He saw a poor widow put in two small copper coins.

original.text: εἶδεν δέ ⸀τινα χήραν πενιχρὰν βάλλουσαν ἐκεῖ ⸂λεπτὰ δύο⸃,

verses.restored: He said, Truly I say to you, this poor widow cast in more than all.

familiar.text: And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all:

modern.text: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “this poor widow has put in more than all the others.

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν· Ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα ⸂ἡ πτωχὴ αὕτη⸃ πλεῖον πάντων ἔβαλεν·

verses.restored: For all these cast in gifts from their abundance, but she from her lack cast in all the living she had.

familiar.text: For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had.

modern.text: For they all contributed out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.” Temple Destruction and Other Signs (Matthew 24:1–8; Mark 13:1–8)

original.text: ⸀πάντες γὰρ οὗτοι ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον εἰς τὰ ⸀δῶρα, αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τοῦ ὑστερήματος αὐτῆς ⸀πάντα τὸν βίον ὃν εἶχεν ἔβαλεν.

verses.restored: As some were speaking about the temple, that it had been adorned with beautiful stones and offerings, he said,

familiar.text: And as some spake of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said,

modern.text: As some of the disciples were remarking how the temple was adorned with beautiful stones and consecrated gifts, Jesus said,

original.text: Καί τινων λεγόντων περὶ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, ὅτι λίθοις καλοῖς καὶ ἀναθήμασιν κεκόσμηται εἶπεν·

verses.restored: These things that you behold, days will come in which not one stone will be left upon another that will not be thrown down.

familiar.text: As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.

modern.text: “As for what you see here, the time will come when not one stone will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”

original.text: Ταῦτα ἃ θεωρεῖτε, ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται λίθος ἐπὶ ⸀λίθῳ ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται.

verses.restored: They questioned him, saying, Teacher, when then will these things be, and what will be the sign when these things are about to happen?

familiar.text: And they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass?

modern.text: “Teacher,” they asked, “when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?”

original.text: Ἐπηρώτησαν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, πότε οὖν ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα γίνεσθαι;

verses.restored: He said, Watch that you are not led astray; for many will come in my name, saying, I am, and, The time has drawn near. Do not go after them.

familiar.text: And he said, Take heed that ye be not deceived: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and the time draweth near: go ye not therefore after them.

modern.text: Jesus answered, “See to it that you are not deceived. For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am He,’ and, ‘The time is near.’ Do not follow them.

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Βλέπετε μὴ πλανηθῆτε· πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου ⸀λέγοντες· Ἐγώ εἰμι καί· Ὁ καιρὸς ἤγγικεν· ⸀μὴ πορευθῆτε ὀπίσω αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: When you hear of wars and disturbances, do not be terrified; for these things must happen first, but the end is not immediately.

familiar.text: But when ye shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by.

modern.text: When you hear of wars and rebellions, do not be alarmed. These things must happen first, but the end is not imminent.” Witnessing to All Nations (Matthew 24:9–14; Mark 13:9–13)

original.text: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκαταστασίας, μὴ πτοηθῆτε· δεῖ γὰρ ταῦτα γενέσθαι πρῶτον, ἀλλʼ οὐκ εὐθέως τὸ τέλος.

verses.restored: Then he said to them, Nation will rise against nation, and reign against reign.

familiar.text: Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom:

modern.text: Then He told them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.

original.text: τότε ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγερθήσεται ἔθνος ἐπʼ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν,

verses.restored: There will be great earthquakes, and in various places famines and plagues; there will be fearful sights and great signs from heaven.

familiar.text: And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven.

modern.text: There will be great earthquakes, famines, and pestilences in various places, along with fearful sights and great signs from heaven.

original.text: σεισμοί τε μεγάλοι ⸂καὶ κατὰ τόπους⸃ ⸂λιμοὶ καὶ λοιμοὶ⸃ ἔσονται, φόβητρά τε καὶ ⸂σημεῖα ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ μεγάλα⸃ ἔσται.

verses.restored: But before all these things, they will lay hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to synagogues and prisons, bringing you before kings and governors because of my name.

familiar.text: But before all these, they shall lay their hands on you, and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name’s sake.

modern.text: But before all this, they will seize you and persecute you. On account of My name they will deliver you to the synagogues and prisons, and they will bring you before kings and governors.

original.text: Πρὸ δὲ τούτων πάντων ἐπιβαλοῦσιν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν καὶ διώξουσιν, παραδιδόντες εἰς ⸀τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ φυλακάς, ⸀ἀπαγομένους ἐπὶ βασιλεῖς καὶ ἡγεμόνας ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου·

verses.restored: It will turn out for you as testimony.

familiar.text: And it shall turn to you for a testimony.

modern.text: This will be your opportunity to serve as witnesses.

original.text: ⸀ἀποβήσεται ὑμῖν εἰς μαρτύριον.

verses.restored: Settle therefore in your hearts not to prepare beforehand to defend yourselves.

familiar.text: Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what ye shall answer:

modern.text: So make up your mind not to worry beforehand how to defend yourselves.

original.text: ⸀θέτε οὖν ⸂ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις⸃ ὑμῶν μὴ προμελετᾶν ἀπολογηθῆναι,

verses.restored: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom that all those opposing you will not be able to withstand or contradict.

familiar.text: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.

modern.text: For I will give you speech and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to resist or contradict.

original.text: ἐγὼ γὰρ δώσω ὑμῖν στόμα καὶ σοφίαν ᾗ οὐ δυνήσονται ⸂ἀντιστῆναι ἢ ἀντειπεῖν⸃ ⸀ἅπαντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: You will be handed over even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends, and some of you they will put to death.

familiar.text: And ye shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of you shall they cause to be put to death.

modern.text: You will be betrayed even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and some of you will be put to death.

original.text: παραδοθήσεσθε δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ γονέων καὶ ⸂ἀδελφῶν καὶ συγγενῶν καὶ φίλων⸃, καὶ θανατώσουσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν,

verses.restored: You will be hated by all because of my name.

familiar.text: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake.

modern.text: And you will be hated by everyone because of My name.

original.text: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.

verses.restored: Yet not a hair from your head will perish.

familiar.text: But there shall not an hair of your head perish.

modern.text: Yet not even a hair of your head will perish.

original.text: καὶ θρὶξ ἐκ τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν οὐ μὴ ἀπόληται.

verses.restored: In your endurance you will gain your lives/souls.

familiar.text: In your patience possess ye your souls.

modern.text: By your patient endurance you will gain your souls. The Destruction of Jerusalem (Matthew 24:15–25; Mark 13:14–23)

original.text: ἐν τῇ ὑπομονῇ ὑμῶν ⸀κτήσασθε τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that her desolation has drawn near.

familiar.text: And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.

modern.text: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, you will know that her desolation is near.

original.text: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε κυκλουμένην ὑπὸ ⸀στρατοπέδων Ἰερουσαλήμ, τότε γνῶτε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ ἐρήμωσις αὐτῆς.

verses.restored: Then those in Judea must flee to the mountains, those in the city must depart, and those in the countryside must not enter her.

familiar.text: Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.

modern.text: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, let those in the city get out, and let those in the country stay out of the city.

original.text: τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη, καὶ οἱ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς ἐκχωρείτωσαν, καὶ οἱ ἐν ταῖς χώραις μὴ εἰσερχέσθωσαν εἰς αὐτήν,

verses.restored: For these are days of justice/reckoning, to fulfill all that has been written.

familiar.text: For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.

modern.text: For these are the days of vengeance, to fulfill all that is written.

original.text: ὅτι ἡμέραι ἐκδικήσεως αὗταί εἰσιν τοῦ πλησθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα.

verses.restored: Woe to those carrying in the womb and nursing infants in those days; for there will be great pressure on the land and wrath for this people.

familiar.text: But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.

modern.text: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people.

original.text: ⸀οὐαὶ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις· ἔσται γὰρ ἀνάγκη μεγάλη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ⸀ὀργὴ τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ,

verses.restored: They will fall by edge of sword and be led captive into all the nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled by nations until the times of nations are fulfilled.

familiar.text: And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

modern.text: They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled. The Return of the Son of Man (Matthew 24:26–31; Mark 13:24–27)

original.text: καὶ πεσοῦνται στόματι μαχαίρης καὶ αἰχμαλωτισθήσονται εἰς ⸂τὰ ἔθνη πάντα⸃, καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἔσται πατουμένη ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν, ἄχρι ⸀οὗ ⸀πληρωθῶσιν καιροὶ ἐθνῶν.

verses.restored: There will be signs in sun, moon, and stars, and on earth distress of nations in perplexity at the roar of sea and waves.

familiar.text: And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring;

modern.text: There will be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and on the earth dismay among the nations, bewildered by the roaring of the sea and the surging of the waves.

original.text: Καὶ ⸀ἔσονται σημεῖα ἐν ἡλίῳ καὶ σελήνῃ καὶ ἄστροις, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς συνοχὴ ἐθνῶν ἐν ἀπορίᾳ ⸀ἤχους θαλάσσης καὶ σάλου,

verses.restored: People fainting from fear and expectation of the things coming upon the inhabited world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

familiar.text: Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.

modern.text: Men will faint from fear and anxiety over what is coming upon the earth, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

original.text: ἀποψυχόντων ἀνθρώπων ἀπὸ φόβου καὶ προσδοκίας τῶν ἐπερχομένων τῇ οἰκουμένῃ, αἱ γὰρ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.

verses.restored: Then they will see the Son of Humanity coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

familiar.text: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

modern.text: At that time they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

original.text: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλῃ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς.

verses.restored: When these things begin to happen, straighten up and lift your heads, because your redemption draws near.

familiar.text: And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.

modern.text: When these things begin to happen, stand up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.” The Lesson of the Fig Tree (Matthew 24:32–35; Mark 13:28–31)

original.text: ἀρχομένων δὲ τούτων γίνεσθαι ἀνακύψατε καὶ ἐπάρατε τὰς κεφαλὰς ὑμῶν, διότι ἐγγίζει ἡ ἀπολύτρωσις ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: He spoke a parable to them: Look at the fig tree and all the trees.

familiar.text: And he spake to them a parable; Behold the fig tree, and all the trees;

modern.text: Then Jesus told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees.

original.text: Καὶ εἶπεν παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς· Ἴδετε τὴν συκῆν καὶ πάντα τὰ δένδρα·

verses.restored: When they put out leaves, seeing it, you know for yourselves that summer is already near.

familiar.text: When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand.

modern.text: When they sprout leaves, you can see for yourselves and know that summer is near.

original.text: ὅταν προβάλωσιν ἤδη, βλέποντες ἀφʼ ἑαυτῶν γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤδη ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·

verses.restored: So also, when you see these things happening, know that the reign of the Divine is near.

familiar.text: So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.

modern.text: So also, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.

original.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ταῦτα γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: this generation will certainly not pass away until all things happen.

familiar.text: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled.

modern.text: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.

original.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.

verses.restored: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.

familiar.text: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

modern.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away. Be Watchful for the Day

original.text: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ ⸀παρελεύσονται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρελεύσονται.

verses.restored: Watch yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with dissipation, drunkenness, and anxieties of life, and that day come upon you suddenly like a trap.

familiar.text: And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.

modern.text: But watch yourselves, or your hearts will be weighed down by dissipation, drunkenness, and the worries of life—and that day will spring upon you suddenly like a snare.

original.text: Προσέχετε δὲ ἑαυτοῖς μήποτε βαρηθῶσιν ⸂ὑμῶν αἱ καρδίαι⸃ ἐν κραιπάλῃ καὶ μέθῃ καὶ μερίμναις βιωτικαῖς, καὶ ⸂ἐπιστῇ ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς αἰφνίδιος⸃ ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη

verses.restored: For it will come upon all those sitting on the face of all the earth.

familiar.text: For as a snare shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth.

modern.text: For it will come upon all who dwell on the face of all the earth.

original.text: ὡς παγίς· ⸂ἐπεισελεύσεται γὰρ⸃ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς.

verses.restored: Stay awake at every time, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things about to happen and to stand before the Son of Humanity.

familiar.text: Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.

modern.text: So keep watch at all times, and pray that you may have the strength to escape all that is about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.”

original.text: ἀγρυπνεῖτε ⸀δὲ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ δεόμενοι ἵνα ⸀κατισχύσητε ἐκφυγεῖν ⸀ταῦτα πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι, καὶ σταθῆναι ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

verses.restored: During the days he was teaching in the temple, and at night he went out and lodged on the mountain called Olivet.

familiar.text: And in the day time he was teaching in the temple; and at night he went out, and abode in the mount that is called the mount of Olives.

modern.text: Every day Jesus taught at the temple, but every evening He went out to spend the night on the Mount of Olives.

original.text: Ἦν δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ⸂ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων⸃, τὰς δὲ νύκτας ἐξερχόμενος ηὐλίζετο εἰς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν·

verses.restored: All the people came early in the morning to him in the temple to hear him.

familiar.text: And all the people came early in the morning to him in the temple, for to hear him.

modern.text: And early in the morning all the people would come to hear Him at the temple.

original.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ὤρθριζεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.
